verdict.line: You lose if you let Darius walk you down into auto-trades where Hemorrhage stacks to five before level 6; you win if you poke with Q (Rupture) and E (Vorpal Spikes) from outside his Apprehend range and carry stacked Feast and a Rocketbelt spike into the mid game.

brief.thesis: Darius' kit is built around closing distance and holding you in melee long enough to stack Hemorrhage to five and enrage; Cho'Gath's entire matchup plan is denying that range with Q (Rupture, 950 range) while chipping damage with E (Vorpal Spikes) on short trades. The 47.7% win rate over 243 games and Darius' lane/solo-kill edge both come from players getting pulled into extended melee they can't win early.

theirWindow.when: his E (Apprehend) is up, you're near 535 range
theirWindow.what: Darius will walk up behind minion cover and throw E to pull you into melee, then stack Hemorrhage and look for Crippling Strike (W) to lock you down for Decimate (Q) and eventually R (Noxian Guillotine).

yourWindow.when: his E and Q (Decimate) are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Step up and auto for free E (Vorpal Spikes) procs, or land Q (Rupture) to knock him up and slow him — this is the only window where he can't punish your approach or hook you back in.

powerCurve.note: Decimate's blade edge wins straight trades
Hemorrhage stacks faster than you can disengage
Rocketbelt burst outscales his flat stats
Stacked Feast health buries his snowball

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: The 49.4% win rate over 251 games (80.2% pick) comes from the mana sustain to actually spam Q (Rupture, 9s cooldown) for poke instead of trading autos you lose.

boots.why: At 49.7% over 175 games (58.7% pick) they're the matchup-correct choice — they blunt both his auto-attacks and the physical Hemorrhage bleed stacking on you.

core.why: Gives you the gap-close/disengage to land your Q-W combo or back off the instant his E lands, matching the 89.5% win rate path over 19 games.
Sustained magic damage plus omnivamp lets you win extended trades once you're ahead on stacks, not just poke.
Closes the speed gap his W (Crippling Strike) slow and E pull create, keeping you in range to land E (Vorpal Spikes) procs.

situational.when: he's building lifesteal and healing through your poke off Decimate's blade hits
lane goes long and you need mana/HP sustain to keep contesting without recalling
you're snowballing Feast stacks and want to lean into raw HP scaling over burst

runes.keystoneWhy: The attack-speed burst lets you stack E (Vorpal Spikes) procs fast in the short trade windows before Hemorrhage climbs toward max stacks — this page sits at 57% win rate (39.1% pick) for a reason.

summoners.why: Exhaust+Flash runs the highest win rate of the tracked combos (63.6%) specifically because it directly answers Darius' all-in — it cuts his damage and slows him right as he commits E or R. Flash+Teleport (49.8%, the majority 62.5% pick) is the safer macro/farming alternative if you'd rather scale uncontested.

playing.title: Hold Q for his Apprehend
playing.detail: Don't walk inside 535 range when his E (Apprehend) is up. Save Q (Rupture) to either answer his pull with a knockup-slow of your own or zone him off before he's in range.

playing.title: Trade on E stacks, not melee
playing.detail: E (Vorpal Spikes) procs on every attack with a 0.5s internal cooldown — poke with auto-E and disengage before his Hemorrhage passive climbs toward five stacks.

playing.title: Track Decimate's cooldown
playing.detail: His Q (Decimate) starts at 9s and drops to 5s by max rank. The window right after he whiffs it is your safest window to step up.

playing.title: Never facecheck his E window
playing.detail: Apprehend's cooldown runs 26s down to 16s at max rank — if it's up and you're in range, assume he's looking for it.

playing.title: Bank R for his all-in, not poke
playing.detail: Feast (R, 60s cooldown, 175 range) deals true damage and grows your max HP on a kill, up to 6 stacks. Use it to end his all-in attempt, not to chip a healthy target.

playing.title: Disengage before max stacks
playing.detail: At 5 Hemorrhage stacks Darius enrages with a massive AD boost. If you're not killing him before that threshold, back off — don't try to out-damage the enrage.

playing.title: Respect the true-damage execute
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine (R) deals true damage scaled by your Hemorrhage stacks and refreshes its cooldown on a kill — never sit at execute range below 6 stacks of bleed.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade patterns are my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Darius close in using (E). Use [Q] carefully to create some distance while focusing on farming lane.
